我是一名执业律师，我代理的当事人甲公司遇到这样一起案件：甲公司于2018年6月在苏州注册成立A公司，认缴出资1亿元，以现金形式实缴出资1亿元。A公司用该笔资金购入了位于天津的一处地产项目。

此后，甲公司于2018年7月在天津注册成立B公司，认缴出资1亿元。甲公司拟让B公司吸收合并A公司，从而将天津地产项目从转至B公司名下以便后续经营。为此，A、B两公司按照法定程序完成了吸收合并，包括天津地产项目在内的全部A公司资产均转至B公司名下。2018年12月1日为合并日，在该日，A公司注销，A公司资产负债表上的所有科目（包括1亿元实收资本）全部平移至B公司资产负债表的对应科目上，B公司的实收资本从0变为1亿元。直至本案争议发生之时，甲公司未再向B公司实缴出资。B公司的工商备案信息显示，该公司的股东认缴出资1亿元，实缴出资为0。

后续因B公司经营恶化，大量欠债，被债权人起诉，但其名下已无可供执行财产，法院裁定终结本次执行。债权人遂提起执行异议程序，申请追加甲公司为被执行人，认为B公司的工商备案信息显示该公司的实缴注册资本为0，甲公司未实缴出资，根据《最高人民法院关于民事执行中变更、追加当事人若干问题的规定》第17条，应在认缴出资范围内对B公司债务承担连带责任。法院裁定支持债权人的追加请求。我方希望提起执行异议之诉，申请法院撤销追加裁定，判决甲公司无需对B公司的债务承担连带责任，我方的核心主张为：B公司的实缴注册资本已因吸收合并A公司而增加1亿元。

我需要你帮我组织起诉思路，具体需要你分析下面的问题：
1. 法院系根据B公司的工商备案信息认定实缴注册资本为0。在认定公司实缴注册资本额时，工商备案信息的证明力如何？如果其他证据显示的公司实缴注册资本额和工商备案的不一样，法院应以什么为准来进行认定？
2. 对方当事人认为，A公司的认缴注册资本1亿元，B公司的认缴注册资本1亿元，那么两公司吸收合并后，B公司的认缴注册资本应该为2亿元而不能是1亿元。对方的这种观点是否正确？
3. 我方核心主张“B公司的实缴注册资本额因吸收合并A公司而增加1亿元”，是否具有法律依据？请尽可能从法律规定、行政规定、司法案例、财务规则等多角度给出依据，尤其是看看是否有案情相同的类案参考案例。

我是一名公司法务，我公司在马来西亚投资房地产业务，作为业主方（发包方）需要与建设工程总承包商签署《建设工程施工合同》，通常，建设工程施工合同会使用FIDIC Yellow Book 2017版本作为合同蓝本。为了最大程度控制公司成本，且严格控制公司房地产项目的建设周期，我公司拟在FIDIC Yellow Book 2017版本的模板基础上，对以下条款进行调整，请你以马来西亚法律专家的身份，审阅以下条款调整意见，并提示我：是否可以合法做如下调整，是否存在法律风险，是否存在会导致合同条款无效或不可执行的法律障碍，是否存在无法使我公司目的实现的法律条款，如有，供应商可以选择何种法律救济。
1. 合同原条款约定，如果存在因业主方原因（如提供资料不准确、未能及时配合移交场地、未能及时支付工程款、未能及时提交需要资料等）造成工程延误，承包商有权主张工期延长、赔偿额外发生的成本加利润的索赔诉求。我公司拟调整约定为：
（1）如发生业主方原因造成的工程延误，承包商有权要求工期延长；或者
（2）如发生业主方原因造成的工程延误，承包商有权要求工期延长并索赔额外发生的成本，即不提及可以索赔对应的利润。
2. 合同原条款约定，如果存在主管当局原因（如主管当局审批不及时、因当地其他活动要求暂时停工等）造成工程延误，承包商有权主张工期延长，且要求业主方补偿由此产生的额外成本。我司拟调整约定为，约定本条款不适用。
3. 合同原条款约定，如果一方违约的，另一方可以要求违约方支付违约赔偿金或者继续履行（Specific Performance）。我公司拟调整约定为，守约方只能要求履约方提供违约赔偿金，排除继续履行的救济方式。
此外，请你分析，即使合同做了上述调整，如果供应商在履约过程中与我公司产生争议，双方诉诸马来西亚法院/AIAC仲裁庭解决争议（适用法律为马来西亚法律），法院/仲裁庭是否可能判决/裁决承包商有权取得损害赔偿？

一家由非澳洲主体在澳大利亚全资设立的公司，主营业务是提供数据中心业务，该业务主要要求该公司建设数据中心机房，并在数据中心内安装机电设备，行程物理的可存储服务器的数据中心空间，并将该数据中心空间租赁给其他公司存放其服务器，过程中提供数据中心业务的公司不会接触到服务器中的数据。现该公司计划在澳大利亚墨尔本租赁两块邻近的已经开发的商业用地开展数据中心业务，并会在不同地块之间铺设光缆以连接两个地块之间的数据中心楼房。根据这段描述，请分析该提供数据中心业务的公司开展上述业务在什么情况下需要获得FIRB审批，在获得FIRB审批前，公司不得开展什么行为？另外，请分析该提供数据中心业务的公司开展上述业务在什么情况下需要获得电信审批？
A基金为某公司股东，且该公司即将完成在美国纳斯达克市场的首次公开发行上市，A基金将在被投公司上市后持有17%的股份。A基金希望在被投公司完成上市后尽快实现退出并完成变现，你是A基金的外部律师，现A基金的法务向你咨询减持需要考虑的法律条款，请提供一份回复涵盖相关的内容。
甲驾驶机动车超速行驶，与行人发生碰撞，该行人当场死亡，甲当即离开事故现场。交警部门根据甲驾驶机动车超速行驶并且在事故发生后弃车逃逸的情节，认定其对事故负主要责任。不考虑其他刑罚减轻从轻或加重从重情节，请判断甲的行为定罪后的量刑区间。

A公司是上市公司，市值300亿，2017年拟非公开发行股票，已完成了所有的监管审批程序。2017年9月，A公司、A公司实际控制人徐某与B公司签署《协议书》，约定B公司以8.89亿元认购A公司非公开发行的股票，可上市流通日为 2018年10月8日。协议中，徐某承诺对B公司的投资款和至少10%的投资收益承担差额补足义务。A公司承担连带责任并提供1.7亿元的保证担保，自收到B公司书面通知起10日内支付，并约定如未按期支付保证金，A公司应自逾期日起，以保证金的数额为基础，按照每日千分之一的标准向B公司支付违约金。A公司并未就该事项发布公告披露。
2018年11月，A公司股票价格持续走低，B公司持有股票现有价值较投资本金及10%投资收益总额差约7000万元，且有损失继续扩大的风险，遂卖出部分股票（亏损约2000万元）并书面通知A公司要求支付保证金1.7亿元。A公司并未按期支付约定保证金，亦未支付违约金。2020年4月，B公司以A公司、徐某为被告，向法院提起民事诉讼，要求A公司及徐某支付承诺的保证金1.7亿元及按照每日千分之一标准计算的违约金6000万元。 
请协助分析以下问题： 
问题1：徐某、A公司与B公司签署的《协议书》效力如何？
问题2：徐某和A公司的赔偿责任又该如何确定？
问题1、2请分别给出类案判决予以辅佐论证。
问题3：假设你是B公司：
1）你是否还可以以A公司未披露保底承诺构成证券虚假陈述为由，主张赔偿？
2）除诉讼途径外，你还可以通过哪些途径或者谈判筹码与徐某、A公司交涉获得赔偿？

你是软件厂商（软件权利人）的外部律师。软件厂商计划推行新的软件销售模式：软件厂商与分销商签署分销合同，仅授予分销商一项销售软件的权利，分销商不得向终端用户授予软件许可，该等软件许可由软件权利人通过《终端用户协议》等方式直接向终端用户授予。分销商可以将从软件权利人处采购标的软件原样转卖给终端用户，从中赚取差价。通常而言软件权利人会要求分销商将软件销售价格控制在一定范围内，但分销商仍然具有一定的定价自由（模式a）。在模式a基础上， 分销商也可以将标的软件与其他软、硬件产品或服务整合后向终端用户提供整合后的产品(“整合产品”)，标的软件在该等整合产品中相对独立，整合产品仍展示软件权利人的品牌（模式b）。分销商还可以结合销售渠道的反馈以及对市场的洞察，在标的软件基础上提供额外的增值服务以满足终端用户的个性化、行业化的需求。在交付方式上，分销商将与其下游终端用户直接进行产品交付及货款结算。该两种模式下，分销商仅有分销标的软件或整合产品的权利而无权授予软件许可，软件许可路径为软件权利人→终端用户。请分析该两种模式下，所涉及的民事法律关系，以及软件厂商作为软件权人所需要考虑的主要法律风险及应对方案？

你是甘肃省定西市某医药零售企业常年法律顾问，你的客户在销售处方药的过程中，由于当地较为落后，药师资源稀缺，故存在由合作执业药师审方中心提供实时在线审方服务的情况，但销售过程都是基于真实用药需求。在国家医疗保障局飞行检查的过程中将此一线索移送公司所在的安定区医疗保障局，对此，公司曾上报《陈述申辩书》，提及“申辩核减远程审方违规金额为60000元，核减理由为“我公司所有门店依法配备专职执业药师，不存在挂证行为，执业药师在营业时间内如因公休、病假、事假等暂时离岗时，均严格依照省药监局相关规定，启用互联网远程审方平台，由合作执业药师审方中心提供实时在线审方服务，确保处方药销售合规，保障患者用药安全”，并参考《甘肃省药品零售连锁企业设置规定(试行)》(甘药监(2022)132号)第二十三条规定。2025年10月16日傍晚，客户收到安定区医疗保障局下发的《行政处罚事先告知书》（安医保罚告字[2025]第XXX号），你的客户还是希望能将远程审方解释为合规行为，核减远程审方相关金额60000元并·免除1倍罚款，据此，请你以客户利益草拟《陈述申报书》。以下是安定区医疗保障局《行政处罚事先告知书》（安医保罚告字[2025]第XXX号）内容：
定西市XX医药有限公司：
2025年3月1日，本机关对你（单位）涉嫌存在执业药师不在岗销售处方药行为予以立案调查。现查明，本机关于2025年2月1日接到国家医疗保障局飞行检查移交资料，2025年1月15日期间，国家医疗保障局基金监管司飞行检查组一行对定西市XX医药有限公司开展了飞行检查，通过查看进销存、处方、考勤表、监控视频、询问相关业务人员、查阅资料等方式，确认该药店存在上述违规行为。在核查过程中，该药店对此次飞检部分违规金额提出申辩并上报《陈述申辩书》，提及“申辩核减远程审方违规金额为60000元，核减理由为“我公司所有门店依法配备专职执业药师，不存在挂证行为，执业药师在营业时间内如因公休、病假、事假等暂时离岗时，均严格依照省药监局相关规定，启用互联网远程审方平台，由合作执业药师审方中心提供实时在线审方服务，确保处方药销售合规，保障患者用药安全”，并参考《甘肃省药品零售连锁企业设置规定(试行)》(甘药监(2022)132号)第二十三条规定。
核查之后确定不予核减，理由如下：一、《甘肃省药品零售连锁企业设置规定(试行)》(甘药监(2022)132号)第二十四条规定“药品零售连锁企业开展远程药学服务，应当自查远程审方条件，认为符合要求后，将自评情况和相关资料分别向省药监局以及连锁门店药品经营许可证发证机关报告，依法配合监督检查”，该药店及合作互联网医院[XX互联网医院]均未能提供相关佐证资料；二、根据《定西市医疗保障定点零售药店服务协议(2023年)》第九条、《定西市医疗保障定点零售药店服务协议(2024年)》第九条、《定西市定点零售药店医疗保障服务协议(2025年)》第八条相关规定（均要求营业时间内有注册地在该药店的执业药师或依法经过资格认定的其他药学技术人员在岗），故不能认定该药店远程审方行为合规；三、该药店对于申辩远程审方部分无明确数据支撑且对违规行为无异议，申辩理由不充分，最终确定此部分违规基金60000元。

本机关认为，你（单位）的上述行为违反了《定西市医疗保障定点零售药店服务协议》（2023—2025年）等相关法规，相关证据包括：1. 《营业执照》《药品经营许可证》及副本、法定代表人身份证复印件各1份（证明主体资格合规）；2. 《现场检查通知书》《现场检查笔录》《飞行检查定点医疗机构问题表》《飞行检查证据清单》、《执业药师注册证（[XXX]）》复印件、[XXX]、[YYY]等相关人员身份证及劳动合同复印件、《医疗机构执业许可证》及副本、《XX市基本医疗保险定点医疗机构医疗服务协议》复印件、《电子处方系统资质》复印件、各类《反馈问题登记表》《药品说明书》《XX市城镇职工基本医疗保险个人账户结算单》《处方笺》、职工排班表、《询问笔录》《检查笔录》等（证明存在违规行为及医保基金损失）；3. 法定代表人身份证、法人授权委托书、被委托人身份证复印件各1份（证明文书签收合法性）；4. 银行回单1份（证明存在从轻或减轻处罚情形）。

鉴于你单位在案件调查期间积极配合执法、如实陈述违法事实并主动提供证据材料，且在飞检结束后（2025年2月28日）上缴违规资金60000元，深刻认识到违法行为，本机关根据《医疗保障基金使用监督管理条例》第三十八条、第三十九条，《中华人民共和国行政处罚法》第三十二条第五项，《甘肃省医疗保障基金使用监督管理行政处罚裁量权适用规则》第十二条、第十五条，以及《甘肃省医疗保障基金使用监督管理行政处罚裁量基准》相关规定，责令你（单位）改正上述违法行为，退回损失的医保基金60000（2025年2月28日已退回60000元），并拟作出如下行政处罚：处造成损失金额60000元1倍的罚款（人民币60000元]）。

根据《行政处罚法》第四十四条、第四十五条规定，你（单位）可在收到本告知书之日起3日内提出陈述、申辩意见，或到安定区医疗保障局进行陈述、申辩；逾期未提出的，视为放弃该权利。根据《行政处罚法》第六十三条、第六十四条规定，你（单位）对上述拟作出的罚款处罚有要求举行听证的权利，可在收到本告知书之日起5日内向本机关提出听证申请；逾期未提出的，视为放弃该权利。

我局接市民举报，其反映参加了某公司在抖音平台举办的视频挑战赛活动，并获得了一张谢霆锋广州演唱会门票，但被举报单位以其发布的参赛视频非原创、存在侵权行为，拒绝为其发放奖品。
问题：

I. Application for leave to appeal

1.  This is a renewed application by the 4th defendant for leave to appeal against the decision of Deputy District Judge ZZ dated 6 December 2024 ('Decision') refusing his appeal to set aside the summary judgment granted by Master WW against him pursuant to the application by the plaintiff. The 4th defendant's application for leave to appeal against the Decision was refused by the Judge on 30 May 2025 ('Leave Decision').

2.  Under Order 59, rule 2A(5)(a) of the Rules of the High Court, Cap. 4A ('RHC'), this Court may determine an interlocutory application without an oral hearing. Having considered the summons, written submissions and the accompanying documents by the parties, we are of the view that it is appropriate to determine the present application on paper without a hearing.

II. Background

3.  The plaintiff is a licensed bank in [Jurisdiction A]. [1]

4.  The 4th defendant is an 18% shareholder of an offshore company named COMPANY B HOLDINGS LTD ('Company B'), which, along with another [Jurisdiction A] company, owns the 1st defendant. [2]

5.  By a facility letter dated 17 November 2017 ('the Facility Letter'), the plaintiff granted an installment loan of \$8,000,000 ('the Loan') to the 1st defendant. In consideration of the Loan, each of the 2nd to 5th defendants executed a Deed of Guarantee dated 22 November 2017 ('the Guarantee'), by which they jointly and severally agreed to pay the plaintiff, on demand in writing, all sums of money owed to the plaintiff by the 1st defendant. [3]

6.  The 1st defendant defaulted on the repayment of the Loan. Notwithstanding the plaintiff's written demands, none of the 2nd to 5th defendants repaid the plaintiff the 1st defendant's indebtedness. [4]

7.  By an action commenced on 10 January 2023, the plaintiff sought to recover the 1st defendant's indebtedness of \$2,352,797.93 from the 2nd to 5th defendants. The plaintiff's claim was denied by the 4th defendant. [5]

8.  The 4th defendant's pleaded case in the Defence and Counterclaim may be summarised as follows [6] :

    1) He claimed that he knew PERSON EE through PERSON EE's wife, the 3rd defendant, in 2015. [7] He and PERSON EE had been in a business relationship since then. [8] In 2017, he agreed to invest in COMPANY C (HOLDING) LIMITED ('Company C') in which the 3rd defendant was a director, and he was told that the 2nd, 3rd and 5th defendants would also be the shareholders of Company C. [9]

    2) In August 2017, at the request of PERSON EE, he signed various documents purportedly for Company C's daily operation. [10]

    3) In November 2017, PERSON EE again asked him to sign some documents purportedly for opening a bank account. On that day, at the carpark of his residence, PERSON EE provided him with some signing pages. He signed on those blank signing pages believing they were for opening a bank account in relation to Company C because 1) PERSON EE assured him that it would be safe for him to sign on them; and 2) he saw the signatures of the 2nd, 3rd and 5th defendants. His signatures on those pages were not witnessed by the 2nd, 3rd or 5th defendants, or any of the plaintiff's representatives. It turned out that he actually signed on the Facility Letter and the Guarantee. [11]

    4) It is the 4th defendant's stance that (1) he had no knowledge that the plaintiff extended the Loan through the Facility Letter; (2) he did not know he became a guarantor for the Loan; and (3) he did not know he was a shareholder of the 1st defendant.

III. The Judge's decision

9.  By his Decision, the Judge found that the plaintiff was entitled to summary judgment. [12] The Judge held that the 4th defendant failed to show why the plaintiff ought to be fixed with any constructive notice of the fraud allegedly practised on him by PERSON EE.

10. The Judge rejected the 4th defendant's evidence on the alleged misrepresentation or undue influence by PERSON EE for being unbelievable and implausible. [13] The Judge did not accept that the plaintiff knew, or ought to have known, the relationship between the 1st and 4th defendants was non-commercial, such that it was put on constructive notice that the Facility Letter and the Guarantee were manifestly disadvantageous to the 4th defendant's interest. [14] The Judge found no evidence of PERSON EE having either actual or ostensible authority from the plaintiff to support the 4th defendant's argument that PERSON EE acted, or should be seen as having acted, as the plaintiff's agent in obtaining his signatures at the carpark. [15]

11. The Judge rejected the 4th defendant's submissions on non est factum and unconscionable bargain, as he failed to overcome the heavy burden on him for invoking the doctrine and to show that his bargaining position was so weak that the law should offer him protection against any alleged unfairness in enforcing the Guarantee against him. [16] In relation to non est factum, the signing page of the Guarantee stated in English and Chinese that it was a deed of guarantee to be signed, sealed and delivered by the persons signing on that page. It was inherently implausible that the 4th defendant did not raise an eyebrow despite how overtly PERSON EE allegedly hindered him from seeing the full signing page.

12. The Judge concluded that the 4th defendant's counterclaim was frivolous and an abuse of the court process, [17] and dismissed his appeal accordingly. [18]

IV. Principles

13. The principles for granting leave to appeal are well established. Under section 63A(2) of the District Court Ordinance, Cap. 336, leave shall not be granted unless the appeal has a reasonable prospect of success, or there is some other reason in the interests of justice that the appeal should be heard. Reasonable prospect involves the notion that the prospects of succeeding must be 'reasonable' and therefore more than 'fanciful', without having to be 'probable'. [19]

V. The 4th defendant's intended grounds of appeal

14. The 4th defendant advances six grounds of appeal in the draft notice of appeal as follows (respectively 'Ground 1' to 'Ground 6') :

    1) The Judge erred in conducting a mini-trial on affidavit as to the credibility of the parties and affirmants to the affirmations and making tentative assessment of the respective chances of success of the parties and the relative strengths of their good or bad faith.

    2) The Judge erred in not drawing any or any sufficient adverse inference from or not considering the absence of PERSON FF as being the weakness of the plaintiff's case when assessing the merits of plaintiff's summary judgment application.

    3) The Judge erred in taking into account irrelevant consideration to determine whether PERSON FF and the plaintiff ought to have known that the 4th defendant's signatures were procured by misrepresentation that PERSON EE practised on him, in particular his interest in Company B and the 1st defendant.

    4) The Judge erred in finding that PERSON FF flouted the plaintiff's guidelines on how documents like the Facility Letter and the Guarantee should be signed and witnessed, but at the same time found that this could not be equated to PERSON FF being complicit in PERSON EE's scam.

    5) The Judge erred in finding that PERSON EE was not an agent of the plaintiff by (1) requiring proof of representation from PERSON EE to the 4th defendant that PERSON EE was authorised by the plaintiff; (2) finding there was no conduct in PERSON EE that could be said to have represented the plaintiff; and (3) not analysing that PERSON EE was an agent of PERSON FF who was the agent of the plaintiff, and thus PERSON EE was the agent of the plaintiff.

    6) The Judge erred when comparing the case of BANK B LTD v COMPANY D LTD & ORS [2024] HKCFI 1859 by (1) failing to take into account that PERSON EE had practised systematically and over an extended period fraud on others, including the 4th defendant, in relation to similar borrowing arrangements concerning the same group of companies; (2) holding that the time at which PERSON EE committed the alleged equitable wrongs on the parties were different in a material and significant manner; and (3) holding that because the Facility Letter and the Guarantee were executed by the 4th defendant at the same time, the likelihood of fraud was lower.

I. Application for leave to appeal

1. This is a renewed application by the 4th defendant for leave to appeal against the decision of Deputy District Judge ZZ dated 6 December 2024 ('Decision') refusing his appeal to set aside the summary judgment granted by Master WW against him pursuant to the application by the plaintiff. The 4th defendant's application for leave to appeal against the Decision was refused by the Judge on 30 May 2025 ('Leave Decision').

2.  Under Order 59, rule 2A(5)(a) of the Rules of the High Court, Cap. 4A ('RHC'), this Court may determine an interlocutory application without an oral hearing. Having considered the summons, written submissions and the accompanying documents by the parties, we are of the view that it is appropriate to determine the present application on paper without a hearing.

II. Background

3. The plaintiff is a licensed bank in [Jurisdiction A]. [1]

4. The 4th defendant is an 18% shareholder of an offshore company named COMPANY B HOLDINGS LTD ('Company B'), which, along with another [Jurisdiction A] company, owns the 1st defendant. [2]

5.  By a facility letter dated 17 November 2017 ('the Facility Letter'), the plaintiff granted an installment loan of \$8,000,000 ('the Loan') to the 1st defendant. In consideration of the Loan, each of the 2nd to 5th defendants executed a Deed of Guarantee dated 22 November 2017 ('the Guarantee'), by which they jointly and severally agreed to pay the plaintiff, on demand in writing, all sums of money owed to the plaintiff by the 1st defendant. [3]

6.  The 1st defendant defaulted on the repayment of the Loan. Notwithstanding the plaintiff's written demands, none of the 2nd to 5th defendants repaid the plaintiff the 1st defendant's indebtedness. [4]

7.  By an action commenced on 10 January 2023, the plaintiff sought to recover the 1st defendant's indebtedness of \$2,352,797.93 from the 2nd to 5th defendants. The plaintiff's claim was denied by the 4th defendant. [5]

8.  The 4th defendant's pleaded case in the Defence and Counterclaim may be summarised as follows [6] :

    1) He claimed that he knew PERSON EE through PERSON EE's wife, the 3rd defendant, in 2015. [7] He and PERSON EE had been in a business relationship since then. [8] In 2017, he agreed to invest in COMPANY C (HOLDING) LIMITED ('Company C') in which the 3rd defendant was a director, and he was told that the 2nd, 3rd and 5th defendants would also be the shareholders of Company C. [9]

    2) In August 2017, at the request of PERSON EE, he signed various documents purportedly for Company C's daily operation. [10]

    3) In November 2017, PERSON EE again asked him to sign some documents purportedly for opening a bank account. On that day, at the carpark of his residence, PERSON EE provided him with some signing pages. He signed on those blank signing pages believing they were for opening a bank account in relation to Company C because 1) PERSON EE assured him that it would be safe for him to sign on them; and 2) he saw the signatures of the 2nd, 3rd and 5th defendants. His signatures on those pages were not witnessed by the 2nd, 3rd or 5th defendants, or any of the plaintiff's representatives. It turned out that he actually signed on the Facility Letter and the Guarantee. [11]

    4) It is the 4th defendant's stance that (1) he had no knowledge that the plaintiff extended the Loan through the Facility Letter; (2) he did not know he became a guarantor for the Loan; and (3) he did not know he was a shareholder of the 1st defendant.

III. The Judge's decision

9.  By his Decision, the Judge found that the plaintiff was entitled to summary judgment. [12] The Judge held that the 4th defendant failed to show why the plaintiff ought to be fixed with any constructive notice of the fraud allegedly practised on him by PERSON EE.

10. The Judge rejected the 4th defendant's evidence on the alleged misrepresentation or undue influence by PERSON EE for being unbelievable and implausible. [13] The Judge did not accept that the plaintiff knew, or ought to have known, the relationship between the 1st and 4th defendants was non-commercial, such that it was put on constructive notice that the Facility Letter and the Guarantee were manifestly disadvantageous to the 4th defendant's interest. [14] The Judge found no evidence of PERSON EE having either actual or ostensible authority from the plaintiff to support the 4th defendant's argument that PERSON EE acted, or should be seen as having acted, as the plaintiff's agent in obtaining his signatures at the carpark. [15]

11. The Judge rejected the 4th defendant's submissions on non est factum and unconscionable bargain, as he failed to overcome the heavy burden on him for invoking the doctrine and to show that his bargaining position was so weak that the law should offer him protection against any alleged unfairness in enforcing the Guarantee against him. [16] In relation to non est factum, the signing page of the Guarantee stated in English and Chinese that it was a deed of guarantee to be signed, sealed and delivered by the persons signing on that page. It was inherently implausible that the 4th defendant did not raise an eyebrow despite how overtly PERSON EE allegedly hindered him from seeing the full signing page.

12. The Judge concluded that the 4th defendant's counterclaim was frivolous and an abuse of the court process, [17] and dismissed his appeal accordingly. [18]

IV. Principles

13. The principles for granting leave to appeal are well established. Under section 63A(2) of the District Court Ordinance, Cap. 336, leave shall not be granted unless the appeal has a reasonable prospect of success, or there is some other reason in the interests of justice that the appeal should be heard. Reasonable prospect involves the notion that the prospects of succeeding must be 'reasonable' and therefore more than 'fanciful', without having to be 'probable'. [19]

V. The 4th defendant's intended grounds of appeal

14. The 4th defendant advances six grounds of appeal in the draft notice of appeal as follows (respectively 'Ground 1' to 'Ground 6') :

    1) The Judge erred in conducting a mini-trial on affidavit as to the credibility of the parties and affirmants to the affirmations and making tentative assessment of the respective chances of success of the parties and the relative strengths of their good or bad faith.

    2) The Judge erred in not drawing any or any sufficient adverse inference from or not considering the absence of PERSON FF as being the weakness of the plaintiff's case when assessing the merits of plaintiff's summary judgment application.

    3) The Judge erred in taking into account irrelevant consideration to determine whether PERSON FF and the plaintiff ought to have known that the 4th defendant's signatures were procured by misrepresentation that PERSON EE practised on him, in particular his interest in Company B and the 1st defendant.

    4) The Judge erred in finding that PERSON FF flouted the plaintiff's guidelines on how documents like the Facility Letter and the Guarantee should be signed and witnessed, but at the same time found that this could not be equated to PERSON FF being complicit in PERSON EE's scam.

    5) The Judge erred in finding that PERSON EE was not an agent of the plaintiff by (1) requiring proof of representation from PERSON EE to the 4th defendant that PERSON EE was authorised by the plaintiff; (2) finding there was no conduct in PERSON EE that could be said to have represented the plaintiff; and (3) not analysing that PERSON EE was an agent of PERSON FF who was the agent of the plaintiff, and thus PERSON EE was the agent of the plaintiff.

    6) The Judge erred when comparing the case of BANK B LTD v COMPANY D LTD & ORS [2024] HKCFI 1859 by (1) failing to take into account that PERSON EE had practised systematically and over an extended period fraud on others, including the 4th defendant, in relation to similar borrowing arrangements concerning the same group of companies; (2) holding that the time at which PERSON EE committed the alleged equitable wrongs on the parties were different in a material and significant manner; and (3) holding that because the Facility Letter and the Guarantee were executed by the 4th defendant at the same time, the likelihood of fraud was lower.

Person A

81.81. The SPC was actually procured by Person F on behalf of D and one Person L (" L ") on behalf of P. The position of L in P is unknown.

She did not say why D had tolerated P's failure to pay D the USD2 million Deposit without any written demands and complaints. 83.83. After the signing of the SPC, L disappeared. Thus, Person A sent Person F to City C to locate him. L told Person F in person that due to the change of P's board, the SPC must be shelved.
84.84. Later, Person A learned from public sources that the share price of P had plummeted and that there was a complete overhaul of the composition of P's board in January 2023. Person F has lost contact with B and L ever since they left P.

She believed that D was entitled to forfeit the deposit of USD6,930,000 since any deposit paid under the SPC would be non-refundable pursuant to the express provision of the SPC. 86.86. Person A reiterated that the parties had only discussed the sale of iron ores and they had never started any in-depth negotiations about the sale of light crude oil.
87.87. Person A then explained how the Instruction Letter came into being. She said in or about November 2022, L called and asked D to issue a letter to inform P that COMPANY E would perform the SPC in D's stead due to D's problem to open a bank account and to prepare an advancement of USD 35 million.

Person A explained that she had not paid any attention to the name of D before her acquisition of D. It was a sheer coincidence that the shell company chosen by Person A bore the same name with that of Company G.
97.97. Person A was also asked extensively about the purported connection between D and Company M, a state-owned enterprise. Person A, nevertheless, insisted that Company M was owned by the State and there was a share entrustment agreement showing the ownership.
98.98. The share entrustment agreement only shows that a person was holding 49% shares in Company M on trust for Person A. No connection with the State is discernible.
99.99. Person A insisted that the USD2 million Deposit was not refundable because the words "deposit" instead of "advance payment" were used to characterise the USD2 million Deposit. Person A explained that the former was non-refundable whereas the latter was refundable. Curiously enough, despite her awareness of the alleged significant distinction between the two terms, in her witness statement, she herself used the latter.
Person F
100.100. Person F was a university graduate having a degree in computer studies. In or about 2021, he worked for an investment company in City B as fund manager and Person A was then the director of that company. Person F worked under her supervision there.
101.101. Person F joined D when it was incorporated in July 2022. He was based in City B. He represented D in the discussion and conclusion of the SPC and he mostly contacted L.
102.102. Regarding the Instruction Letter, L called him and asked for the Instruction Letter to be issued to P to enable P to raise fund for the joint development project. L gave the name of COMPANY E to him.
103.103. After the signing of the SPC, he could not find L. Then Person A instructed him to come to City C to look for him. L was finally located and he told Person F that the SPC had to be shelved due to an imminent change of the board's composition.
104.104. Person F confirmed that the purported signatures of Person A in the Disputed Agreements do not belong to Person A and the rectangular company chop appearing in the Termination Agreements was different from D's rectangular company chop.
105.105. He further indicated that the round company chop appearing in the Cooperation Agreement was different from D's only round company chop, a copy of which was exhibited to the witness statement of Person A.
106.106. Lastly, Person F stated that he had never taken part in any discussion in respect of the Disputed Agreements.
Applicable legal principles
107.107. The key issue is the authenticity of the Disputed Agreements and it turns on the credibility of the witnesses.
108.108. Mr G and Mr H refer to the following relevant authorities which provide useful guidelines for the assessment of credibility of witnesses.
109.109. In Case A (unreported, HCA 2020-COMM-1234, 8.4.2021) at §§77 to 83, Judge X stated:-
(a) Contemporaneous written documents and documents which came into existence before the problems in question emerged are of the greatest importance in assessing credibility.
(b) The Court should attach importance to the inherent likelihood or unlikelihood of any event having happened, or the apparent logic of such events.
(c) The Court may take into account the consistency of the witness' evidence having regard to the undisputed or indisputable evidence, and the internal consistency of the witness' evidence.
(d) The Court should exercise care in drawing conclusions about truthfulness and reliability solely or largely from the appearance or demeanour of a witness or from the assessment of a witness' character.
(e) The Court should also test a witness' credibility by reference to objective facts which are proven independently of their testimony, taking into account their motives and to the overall probabilities.
110.110. In Case B [2020], Judge Y at §73 said this,
"It is trite law that where there has been no satisfactory explanation for the absence of documents which should on the evidence be in existence, the court is entitled to draw an adverse inference against the party who should be in possession of such documents that the party has something to hide."
111.111. In Case C [2001] 2 , Judge Z applied the maxim omina praesumuntur contra spoliatorem (" the Maxim ") at pp.365-366. In simple terms, the Maxim is that in general the failure to bring before the court some documents or witnesses from which/whom relevant evidence could emanate, the most natural inference to be drawn is that the party fears to do so and the fear is that such documents or witnesses, if brought, would have exposed facts unfavourable to the party. The non-production of evidence that would naturally have been produced by an honest and therefore fearless claimant permits the inference that its tenor is unfavourable to the party's cause.
112.112. Mr G draws my particular attention to Case D (2005) 8 at §§180-184, 626 for the correct approach to the determination of allegations of forgery:
(a) Although the Plaintiff (as proponent of the disputed documents) bear the legal burden of proof to establish authenticity of the disputed documents, the Defendant bears the evidential burden of adducing sufficiently cogent and probative evidence to raise the issue of forgery. Hence, in approaching the issue (which involves a serious allegation), the Court must be satisfied that the standard of cogency of the evidence is sufficient to raise a case of forgery.
(b) When weighing up and assessing the probabilities in relation to the evidence adduced by the respondent as evidence of forgery, the Court must bear in mind the seriousness of the misconduct alleged, recognising that it carries and inherent degree of improbability.

鉴定式案例分析方法是一种源自德国的法律案例分析方法，近年来已深入法律教学与实践当中，在刑法、民法等领域广泛应用。在刑法案例的分析中，所谓鉴定式分析法，亦称归入法：先以假设抛出问题作为分析的起点，然后开始逐步、逐要件地进行确认，最后得出假设是否成立的结论。具体到刑法案例分析领域，一般来说，鉴定式分析可分为五个步骤：划分事实单元→寻找刑法规范→选定审查思路→展开涵摄分析→得出最终结论。具体而言，步骤是：
1、划分事实单元：将案件事实按时间顺序、行为与结果的关联性等划分为独立单元，确保每个单元包含一个完整的行为及对应结果。
2、寻找刑法规范：根据事实单元，全面检索可能适用的刑法条文，包括罪名、特别法与普通法的关系，以及相关法律拟制条款等。
3、选定审查思路：此处可采用两阶层、三阶层、四要件等不同犯罪体系论，关键在于事实单元审查顺序的合理安排（通常按照不同主体的行为顺序）以及犯罪构成要件、责任要素等方面的的有序审查。

Justice A (giving the Judgment of the Court):

INTRODUCTION

1.  1. This is the Defendant's appeal against the judgment of Judge B (as he then was) dated 31 March 2023, whereby it was adjudged that the Defendant was liable to repay to the Plaintiff a loan in the total sum of local currency units 42,850,000 together with interest thereon at the rate of 48% per annum from the respective dates on which various tranches of the loan were advanced to the Defendant until payment.

2.  2. As will be seen, the principal issue which arises for determination in this appeal is what an oral loan agreement made in the Jurisdiction which provides for interest on the loan to be paid at the "maximum rate as the law permitted" means in the circumstances of the present case.

    [BASIC FACTS]

3.  3. The background facts of this case have been set out in the written judgment of the Judge dated 31 March 2023 (" the Judgment "). For the purpose of disposing of the present appeal, the following brief summary should suffice.

4.  4. The Plaintiff (" the Plaintiff ") was a businessman with connections both in the Neighboring Jurisdiction and the Other Jurisdiction including, in the latter case, those in the gaming industry.

5.  5. The Defendant, the Charitable Foundation Limited (" the Foundation "), is a company incorporated in the Jurisdiction and limited by guarantee set up in 1988 by the late the Deceased (" the Deceased ") and her late husband (" the Deceased's Husband "). Prior to their respective deaths, the Deceased and the Deceased's Husband were in control of the Business Group. Although the business of the Foundation was said to be the granting of financial support for charity and community benefits, as found by the Judge, its sources of donation mostly came from within the Business Group, and it was effectively a conduit through which funds were received and donated to designated donees on the Deceased's behalf.

6.  6. After the passing of the Deceased in April 2007, the board of governors of the Foundation consisted of three siblings of the Deceased, including the Defendant's Representative A (" the Defendant's Representative A ") and two younger sisters, and a number of employees of the Business Group, including the Defendant's Representative B (" the Defendant's Representative B "), a qualified accountant who was, at the material time, the chief financial officer of the Business Group. At that time, the chief executive officer of the Business Group was the Group CEO (" the Group CEO ").

7.  7. Since 2007, the Foundation had been embroiled in a high profile litigation with the Opposing Party concerning the estate of the Deceased (Probate Case 8/2007, " the Probate Action "). The Foundation, under the control of the Defendant's Representative A siblings, took the stance that it was the beneficial owner of the estate of the Deceased, including the Business Group, and the then understanding of those concerned was that success in the Probate Action would put the Defendant's Representative A siblings in control of the Foundation as well as the Business Group [1] .

8.  8. By early 2009, the Foundation had already spent over local currency units 50 million on legal costs in the Probate Action, and was in need of substantial further funds for the trial of the action [2] , which had been set down for hearing in May 2009 with an estimated length of some 40 days. The Foundation was not able to look to the Business Group for funds to finance the litigation because the estate of the Deceased had been put under the control of the administrators pendente lite since the end of 2007. Institutional borrowing was not feasible in the absence of fixed assets or substantial income-producing business of the Foundation [3] . In short, the Foundation was in urgent need of funding by early 2009.

9.  9. In late 2008/early 2009, the late the Intermediary A (" the Intermediary A "), a Jurisdiction businessman and a member of the political advisory body, was apparently assisting the Defendant's Representative A/the Foundation to explore urgent funding for the Probate Action. the Intermediary A and the Group CEO were friends of the Intermediary B (" the Intermediary B "), a Jurisdiction businessman. the Intermediary B was a friend and business partner of the Plaintiff, while the Plaintiff was acquainted with the Intermediary A.

10. 10. According to the Plaintiff, it was through the introduction of the Intermediary A that he came to meet the Defendant's Representative A in early 2009. the Plaintiff said that he reached an oral agreement (" the Loan Agreement ") with the Defendant's Representative A on behalf of the Foundation in the course of three meetings in the Jurisdiction in early 2009 to advance a loan in the region of local currency units 40 million with interest at the maximum rate permitted by law to the Foundation. We shall come back to the issue of the rate of interest later in this judgment.

11. 11. the Plaintiff also said that the original agreement with the Defendant's Representative A was that the loan and interest thereon were to be repaid by July 2009, but the date of repayment was subsequently extended by mutual agreement such that the loan and interest would be repayable on demand only after the conclusion of the Probate Action.

12. 12. Between March and June 2009, the Plaintiff paid or caused to be paid the total sum of local currency units 42,850,000 by 9 tranches into the bank account of the Foundation with the Bank:

13. 13. the Plaintiff said that, out of the local currency units 42,850,000 advanced to the Foundation, he personally provided local currency units 20,000,000, and borrowed the balance in the sum of local currency units 22,850,000 from his friends or business associates at the monthly interest rate of 3% per annum for a term of 6 months.

14. 14. In February 2010, Justice C (as Justice C then was) gave a judgment in favour of the Foundation and against the Opposing Party in the Probate Action. The subsequent appeals by the Opposing Party against Justice C's judgment were unsuccessful. The dispute between the Opposing Party and the Foundation concerning the estate of the Deceased came to a final conclusion when the Appeal Committee of the Court of Final Appeal refused to grant the Opposing Party leave to appeal on 28 October 2011 (Final Appeal Case 20/2011).

15. 15. In August 2014, the Plaintiff through his solicitors formally demanded the Foundation for repayment of the loan and interest thereon. Consequent upon the failure of the Foundation to satisfy the demand, on 13 April 2015, the Plaintiff commenced the present action against the Foundation seeking to recover the outstanding loan and interest thereon. An alternative claim based on unjust enrichment was also advanced by the Plaintiff against the Foundation in the action.

16. 16. The Foundation resisted the Plaintiff's action, primarily on the basis that the monies which it received between March and June 2009 as summarized in §12 above were "unconditional donations" from the payors. It was also the Foundation's case that although the Defendant's Representative A once had a casual meeting with the Plaintiff through the introduction of the Group CEO in or about 2008 in the City in the Neighboring Jurisdiction, " the Defendant's Representative A had never indicated and/or discussed the making of any donation or any form of alleged financial assistance to be made by [the Plaintiff] to [the Foundation] whether before, during and/or after the said meeting ", that " [n]one of the other Governors of [the Foundation] have ever discussed with [the Plaintiff] nor been contacted by him in relation to any alleged loan to be granted or any donation to be made by [the Plaintiff] to [the Foundation] ", and the Foundation had " never entered into any kind of loan agreement whatsoever, whether verbal or written, with [the Plaintiff] " [4] .

    [THE JUDGMENT]

17. 17. The trial of this action came before the Judge in January 2022. At the trial, the Plaintiff and the Intermediary B gave evidence on the Plaintiff's side, while the Defendant's Representative A and the Defendant's Representative B gave evidence on the Defendant's side.

18. 18. On 31 March 2023, the Judge gave the Judgment, finding in favour of the Plaintiff against the Foundation. The Judge evaluated the conflicting evidence of the parties and came to the following conclusion on the issue of the Loan Agreement at §64 of the Judgment:

    "Testing the oral evidence in line with the principles summarised from the outset, I prefer the evidence adduced on behalf of the Plaintiff to that of the Defendant's Representative A where they conflict. I find that there was in fact the oral loan agreement between the Plaintiff and the Defendant's Representative A on behalf of the Foundation whereby loans would be extended and repayable on demand after the conclusion of the Probate Action, and pursuant to that the various sums of money were caused by the Plaintiff to be deposited into the Foundation..."

19. 19. On the issue of interest, the Judge held that the contractual rate of interest should be 48% per annum. We shall come back to the Judge's reasoning for this holding later when we consider the Foundation's appeal concerning the issue of interest.

20. 20. Having reached the above conclusions, the Judge considered that the Plaintiff was entitled to recover the amount claimed as a loan and did not have to rely on the alternative cause of action based on unjust enrichment. Nevertheless, the Judge dealt with the unjust enrichment claim briefly, holding that the Foundation's key contention that it had materially altered its position by acting on the belief that the sums received from the Plaintiff were unconditional donations and spending the same on legal costs in the Probate Action should be rejected.

21. 21. On the basis of the aforesaid findings, the Judge gave judgment for the Plaintiff against the Foundation for the sum of local currency units 42,850,000 with interest at the rate of 48% per annum on the sums accruing from their respective drawdown dates as set out in the table at §12 above until payment.

    [THE APPEAL AND RESPONDENT'S NOTICE]

22. 22. The Foundation's Notice of Appeal against the judgment dated 27 April 2023 contains 3 grounds:

    (1) Ground 1 contends that the Judge's holding that the Foundation should pay interest at 48% per annum is unsustainable as a matter of law;

    (2) Ground 2 contends that any term to the effect that the interest rate should be "the maximum rate as the law permitted" is, as a matter of law, void for uncertainty; and

    (3) Ground 3 contends that the Judge's finding that the Loan Agreement was proved is plainly wrong, in that he had overlooked various matters referred to at §3(a) to (f) of the Notice of Appeal, and no reasonable judge could have reached such finding in light of those matters.

23. 23. the Plaintiff's Respondent's Notice dated 18 May 2023 also contains 3 grounds. In Counsel for the Plaintiff's Respondent's Skeleton Argument on Cross-Appeal dated 11 April 2025, Counsel for the Plaintiff confirms that the Plaintiff would not pursue Grounds 1 and 2. The remaining Ground 3 argues that if the Loan Agreement is found to be void or unenforceable as contended by the Foundation on appeal, the Plaintiff's unjust enrichment claim should be allowed such that the Foundation shall in any event pay local currency units 42,850,000 to the Plaintiff.

## 已安装 Skill 与工作目录

必须先阅读并实际遵循 `finance-ic-memo` Skill：

- 名称：`finance-ic-memo`
- 入口：`/skills/finance-ic-memo/SKILL.md`
- Skill 脚本相对路径基准：`/skills/finance-ic-memo/`
- 来源门禁脚本：`/skills/finance-ic-memo/scripts/source_gate.py`

Skill 中的来源优先级、稀释计算、投决阈值、异常处理和脱敏规则是本任务的业务规则。仅提及 Skill 不算完成；请按 Skill 的 SOP 运行来源门禁并保留结果。

## 必交付物

所有交付物只能写入 `/app/output/`，文件名必须逐字一致。下面只规定交付结构和覆盖范围；所有金额、比例、日期、状态和公式必须由 `/app/input_files/` 的证据恢复，题面不提供目标数值。

1. `FIN-WF-VAL-001_investment_memo.md`：中文投资委员会备忘录。必须包含执行摘要、来源冲突与处理、经营表现、交易结构、可比公司估值、投决门禁、风险和待确认事项。金额以人民币元展示，百分比至少保留 1 位小数，倍数保留 1 位小数。
2. `FIN-WF-VAL-001_valuation_model.csv`：可复核估值模型。必须包含 normalized_inputs、cap_table、transaction、comps、valuation、sensitivity、gates 七个 section；每行包含 `section,metric,value,unit,formula,source` 六列。
3. `FIN-WF-VAL-001_ic_risk_register.csv`：风险登记表。表头必须为 `risk_id,risk_category,evidence,metric,severity,mitigation`，至少 10 条，覆盖客户集中度、应收账款账龄、汇率敞口、原材料价格、股权口径冲突、债务到期、供应商集中度、IP 权属、数据合规、关联交易、ESG 或保险中的至少 10 类；关键数字要落到源文件行/字段，并在表中保留一个可复算的 EBITDA 公式。
4. `FIN-WF-VAL-001_source_reconciliation.csv`：来源对账表。表头必须为 `field,signed_source,draft_value,signed_value,adopted_value,decision,evidence`，逐项记录草稿与签署版的关键冲突，并说明采用、双情景或暂停的理由。
5. `FIN-WF-VAL-001_diligence_questions.csv`：尽调问题清单。表头必须为 `question_id,workstream,question,evidence_gap,owner,priority,blocking,dependency`，至少 12 条，覆盖交易、财务、客户、供应链、法务、合规、IP、关联交易、ESG 和保险。
6. `FIN-WF-VAL-001_ic_decision_matrix.csv`：投决门禁矩阵。表头必须为 `gate_id,gate,threshold,actual,status,evidence,precondition,condition_to_close`，至少 8 条，明确 PASS/FAIL/PAUSED 及前置依赖；status 必须服从证据充分性，而不是用单方材料推断。
7. `FIN-WF-VAL-001_operating_evidence_bridge.csv`：跨源经营证据桥。表头必须为 `section,metric,value,unit,formula,source,decision,downstream_dependency`；必须包含 `performance`、`cohort_product`、`pipeline_budget`、`cash_reconciliation` 四个 section，并分别回查财务、产品与 cohort、销售管线与预算、月度现金流。桥接表必须区分实际、计划、情景和待确认值。
8. `FIN-WF-VAL-001_closing_conditions_tracker.csv`：交割条件追踪表。表头必须为 `condition_id,condition,source_gap,owner,blocking,dependency,status,required_evidence,linked_gate`，至少 10 条，覆盖材料中出现的条款冲突、现金冲突、IP 权属、跨境 telemetry、关联交易、公允性、可转债信息缺口、客户同意、保险、供应商续约和应收回款证据，并把上游分支依赖传播到 gate。

## 结构化核验与推导要求（仍只能写上述 8 个文件）

- 交易结构、fully diluted 股权、primary/secondary、签署版清算优先权、可比公司筛选、现金流 checksum、预算/headcount、客户换汇和管线覆盖都必须在相应 CSV 中逐行落表，并在 memo 中给出公式及来源行/字段。`liquidation_waterfall.csv` 只能作为待排除的示例，不能覆盖签署版条款。
- 必须逐项列出债务工具和其可计算性。对于材料没有提供转换价格或转换股数的工具，不得补造假设；应在估值、风险、门禁和交割条件中保持 `NOT_COMPUTABLE` 或等价的暂停状态。
- `ConvertibleBridge` 的缺失转换价格或转换股数只阻断 post-conversion fully diluted shares、ownership、MOIC 以及明确依赖转换后股数的 runway 情景；不得据此否定已知本金下、按两份 rank-1 期末现金口径计算的基础 cash runway。基础 runway 仍须给出 A/B 双情景，转换后受影响的 runway 可标记为 `PAUSED` 或 `NOT_COMPUTABLE`。
- 经营证据桥必须把概率加权管线、市场规模和预算收入与已实现收入分开，并同时呈现增长分母不同的覆盖率；必须识别 headcount 计划之间的口径差异并传播为待核验事项。
- 现金流要逐月校验 opening、inflow、outflow、capex、debt service 和 closing 的等式，并把 checksum 与签署版期末现金口径分开。遇到两个同等级来源冲突时，所有依赖净债务、股权价值、runway、burn sensitivity 和投决建议的下游字段必须保留双情景或暂停。
- source gate 必须列出 active/inactive roster、实际使用的 rank-1 文件和被排除记录；草稿只能作为冲突证据，不能静默覆盖签署版。
- 输出 CSV 中每个 `section,metric` 组合必须唯一；金额、股数、比例和状态必须使用与 `data_dictionary.md` 一致的单位。memo 必须有独立的“上游事实→下游字段→交付物”依赖表和关键数字证据索引。

## 受控错误机制与证据门禁

- `FAIL` 仅用于材料已经证明不满足阈值或权利状态已确定不合格；投决矩阵中的待补证门禁必须使用 `PAUSED` 或 `NOT_COMPUTABLE`，并在交割条件/风险表中写出责任人、解锁证据、blocking 和 linked gate。`OPEN` 只能表示尚未进入投决判定的尽调问题，不能作为已完成门禁的状态。关联交易公允性缺口必须保持交割阻塞属性。
- cash conflict 与 signed price/fully-diluted price 不一致是两个独立的 rank-1 冲突，必须分别在 source reconciliation 中恢复，并把各自影响传播到估值、风险、门禁、交割条件和 memo；不得把一个冲突的 checksum、草稿值或单点选择冒充最终答案。
- 所有上游状态和派生数值必须在 memo、valuation_model、risk_register、decision_matrix、source_reconciliation、closing_tracker 之间一致；任何一处把未决项恢复成无条件 PASS 或已确认 FAIL，均视为错误传播。

## 硬约束与禁止事项

- 交付物只能落在 `/app/output/`；不得修改 `/app/input_files/`，不得在输出中复制输入文件。
- 必须使用签署版条款和签署版股权表作为交易结构主口径，同时披露草稿冲突；不得把 `primary`、`secondary` 或期权池漏算、重复计算或混为一谈。
- 必须把美元客户收入换算成人民币，过滤 inactive 记录，计算 Top-1 客户占比；输出不得出现客户姓名、手机号、税号或可还原这些字段的原始值。
- 可比公司估值必须列出实际入选的至少 3 家公司、排除理由和中位数倍数；不得把 `status=inactive` 或增长率超过 40% 的公司纳入中位数。
- 必须展示 fully diluted shares、primary 新发股数、secondary 转让股数、交割后总股数和新投资人总持股比例，并明确公司实际收到的现金只包括 primary。
- 不得编造输入中没有的汇率、阈值、财务数据、监管结论或外部市场事实。无法由材料支持的内容写为待确认事项。
- 交付前自行扫描 `/app/output/`，确认没有手机号、税号、原始客户姓名和临时文件。
- 不得把 sales pipeline 的概率加权金额当作 2025 已实现收入；不得把 market landscape 的 TAM 当作公司收入；不得把 liquidation waterfall 的示例结果当作签署条款。
- 尽调问题必须能回指具体证据缺口，并标明谁负责、是否阻塞交割以及依赖哪个上游分支。
- 经营证据桥不得把 pipeline、TAM 或预算收入当作已实现收入；现金冲突必须保留双情景并暂停依赖 runway、净债务和股权价值的结论。
- 交割条件追踪表必须逐行有责任人、blocking、dependency 和 required_evidence；不得只在备忘录中概括条件。

## 完成条件

八个文件均存在且可读取；模型七个 section 和经营证据桥四个 section 齐全；备忘录、模型、风险登记、来源对账、尽调问题、投决矩阵和交割条件追踪表使用同一套采用口径；所有关键数字可从输入文件追溯，PII 已脱敏，且没有修改源文件。

（四）审查事项编号为「审查事项1」至「审查事项6」，依次对应方案第一条至方案第六条，正文与表格中一一对应、连续无跳号无重号；
（五）整改建议分项用「（1）（2）（3）」；
（六）整体风险评估结论章节须在「可按现方案实施」「须完成整改后方可实施」「不建议实施」三档中择一并说明理由；
（七）「假设与限制」与「未发表意见事项」各自独立成节；
（九）版式上标题居中，风险等级的视觉标记（底色或者加粗）与文字定级一致，表格不应跨页断裂致表头丢失，整改建议与同一行的风险条目对齐可读，整体风险评估结论独立成节并有小标题。
交付结构：仅交付一个可正常打开的.docx文件，全部内容置于该文件内，不应拆分为多个文件，不应交付为.doc、.pdf或者纯文本；各栏位均须填写具体内容，不应出现＿或者____等空白待填符号，不应出现「XX年XX月」这类未填日期。

请帮我以一份真实结案卷宗为素材，编写一道高难度的案例分析题并附参考答案，使答题者必须在多条相互冲突的救济路径之间作出有依据的取舍，而不是简单罗列法条。

背景信息：

为什么做这件事：用于检验法律从业者处理复杂实务问题的能力，重点考查对裁判逻辑的复盘、程序期限的把控、路径冲突的识别，以及信息不足时的判断方法。
目标受众：具备法律职业资格、有一定诉讼经验的律师或法务，熟悉《民法典》《公司法》《民事诉讼法》的基本规则，但不一定处理过检察监督、隐名股东执行异议、个人破产等交叉问题。
相关素材：附件一是一份合同纠纷案的律所结案归档扫描件，含一审、二审判决，再审裁定，委托合同和收费记录；附件二是一份风格参考题（跨境重组决策备忘录）。
约束条件：

文字风格贴近执业律师的真实写法，避免模板化表述；
交付为Word文档，包含题干、任务、考点和参考答案四部分。

# FY2025 受控口径决策登记

你是晨星消费科技有限公司的经营分析师。请只使用容器中的 `/app/input_files/` 两份材料：`operating_snapshot_template.xlsx` 和 `bundle_total_control.csv`。输出一份可审计的决策登记。

## 产出要求

只生成容器 `/app/output/weakness-W11-001_decision_register.csv`，字段必须为：`item_id, claim, evidence, decision, formal_value, calculation, status`。`formal_value` 填写正式口径的计算结果或明确的 `N/A`；`calculation` 填写模板中保留的原公式（或对直接控制值、缺失值和拒绝值的简短计算/处理说明）。登记计算结果不等于改写工作簿公式，公式必须保留在 `calculation` 列。

登记必须恰好包含以下 11 个 item_id，各出现一次且不得增加其他行：REV_ADJ、REV_TOTAL、GROSS_MARGIN、NET_MARGIN、CASH_ADJ、CASH_TOTAL、CONCENTRATION、CASH_2024、NARRATIVE_ADJ、NARRATIVE_TOTAL、NARRATIVE_CASH。它们分别覆盖收入调整、调整后收入、毛利率、净利润率、经营现金调整、经营现金总额、客户集中度、2024 经营现金和三个 Narrative 单元格。

## 硬约束

允许的 decision 只有 use_controlled_value、preserve_formula、leave_NA 和 reject_as_formal_source；允许的 status 只有 controlled、unsupported 和 rejected。

`bundle_total_control.csv` 和模板 Controls 中的 OV-Y12、OV-Y10 只支持 250 CNY k；不得采用 Narrative 中的 500 或 120500。正式结果分别为：调整后收入 120250 CNY k、毛利率 40.1%、净利润率 8.7%、经营现金总额 6950 CNY k、客户集中度 29.9%。对应模板公式必须原样记录在 `calculation` 列：`=B4+B5`、`IFERROR((B6-B7)/B6, N/A)`、`IFERROR(B9/B6, N/A)`、`=B11+B12`、`IFERROR(B14/B6, N/A)`。2024 经营现金缺少明细，必须保持 N/A。

Narrative!B4、B5、B6 只能登记为 `reject_as_formal_source`，不得进入正式口径。不得使用外部数据、邻近数值或未经支持的假设，不得把公式结果改成硬编码值。

人脸识别项目初审意见复核与上线门禁

【任务】
你是企业法务负责人。某平台考虑在登录、客服质检、门禁三个场景使用可能涉及人脸的技术，并考虑让外部供应商参与处理。请仅依据题目附件中的法律来源与24条初审意见，逐条复核并形成上线决策备忘录。不得假设系统已上线或补写业务事实，不得引用输入外的法律、案例、罚款或监管口径。

【输出要求】
只生成简体中文 Markdown 备忘录。必须包含：执行结论、逐条复核表、场景决策、供应商角色分流、证据与影响评估门禁、分阶段整改与验收、引用来源。O01-O24各自单独成行，列为：ID | 处置 | 法律理由与锚点 | 证据缺口/修订文本 | 上线影响。
处置只能为：保留、限缩、待证、删除；上线影响只能为：硬阻断、条件门禁、无独立影响。

# 离职员工竞业限制安排复核与决策备忘录

你是某科技企业的企业法务负责人。人力资源团队希望决定是否继续履行、解除或执行一份拟议中的离职员工竞业限制安排。请只依据 `/app/input_files/[legal_sources.md](http://legal_sources.md)`、`/app/input_files/[case_materials.md](http://case_materials.md)` 和 `/app/input_files/[preliminary_opinions.md](http://preliminary_opinions.md)`，形成供法务负责人使用的法律备忘录。不得把脱敏业务摘要或初审意见当作已证事实，不得引用输入外的法律、司法解释、案例、地方标准、处罚或监管口径。

## 输出与文件

- 只生成 `/app/output/[competition_memo.md](http://competition_memo.md)`，简体中文 Markdown。
- 建议 3000-4500 字；表格可以较长，但不得拆成多个文件。
- 法律引用必须使用 `[legal_sources.md](http://legal_sources.md)` 中的 `[S1-*]` 锚点；每个关键结论都要能追溯到条文或明确标注待证。
- 必须包含以下七个标题：`执行结论`、`事实边界`、`逐条复核表`、`继续/解除决策`、`证据与流程门禁`、`风险与整改`、`引用来源`。

## 逐条复核表

- 对 O01-O28 每条单独成行，不得合并、缺号或改号。
- 固定列为：`ID | 处置 | 法律理由与锚点 | 证据缺口/修订文本 | 决策影响`。
- `处置`只能从 `保留`、`限缩`、`待证`、`删除` 中选择。整体方向正确但条件不全的意见应当`限缩`，不能误作`保留`；输入材料无法证明事实或法律适用边界的事项应当`待证`，不能为了给出结论而补写事实。
- `法律理由与锚点`必须说明为什么选择该处置，不得只复述原意见；必须分别核对人员资格、书面约定、范围/地域/期限、经济补偿和实际违约，不能用其中一项替代另一项。
- `证据缺口/修订文本`：`待证`必须列出决定性证据；`限缩`必须给出一句可替换的准确表述；`删除`必须指出冲突或缺失并给出纠偏结论；`保留`必须写明适用边界。
- `决策影响`只能从 `硬阻断`、`条件门禁`、`无独立影响` 中选择。

## 综合分析要求

1. `继续/解除决策` 分别处理继续履行竞业限制、解除竞业限制、启动违约追偿、准备争议应诉四个决策，并且每项只能给出 `暂缓`、`有条件推进` 或 `不适用待核实`，同时列出控制该结论的 O 项。
2. 清楚区分人员资格、约定成立、范围地域期限、经济补偿和违约事实五个问题。不得以岗位名称、付款意愿或单方邮件替代书面约定和事实证据。
3. `证据与流程门禁` 至少列出：人员类别和保密义务、劳动合同/保密协议/竞业条款原件、范围地域期限、补偿计算与支付、竞争者和实际违约、解除或争议程序材料；每项写责任角色、证据产物、完成时点和阻断条件。
4. `风险与整改` 按 P0/P1/P2 列责任角色、证据产物、可复核验收标准，并说明哪些事项在证据完成前不得继续履行或追偿。
5. 只能复述脱敏占位符，不得输出或推断真实个人/企业标识、账号、凭证、联系方式、工资数额、日期或非公开事实。


【题目附件】
请结合“01_题目附件”目录中的三份脱敏输入材料完成题目。输入材料仅用于本题，不得将待核实内容当作已证事实。
